open_points.subject: A17 configuration-file re-read
open_points.text: A17 says “the checks and the read use that one opened file, so the file checked is the file read,” while A16 rule 2 says the kernel first reads the file to compare its digest and, when it differs, “re-reads it,” with exactly four checks applying to that re-read.
open_points.question: When A16 refreshes the token list, must hashing, security checks and parsing use one securely opened descriptor, or may the comparison and parsing use separate opens?
options: Open once per request and use the same checked descriptor for hashing and parsing
Open once to compare and again to parse, checking both opened files
Apply the one-descriptor rule only at startup
open_points.default_guess: Open once per request and use that checked descriptor for both hashing and parsing.

open_points.subject: A17 security checks during configuration refresh
open_points.text: A17 requires the configuration file to be regular, non-symlink, owned by the kernel user and inaccessible to group or others, and defines component-by-component opening; A16 says “Exactly four checks apply to a re-read,” and those four omit ownership, mode, regular-file and path-component checks.
open_points.question: Which A17 path, type, ownership and permission requirements are revalidated when the configuration is read again for token changes, and what happens if they cease to hold after startup?
options: Reapply every A17 opening and file-security check and refuse every request while any fails
Use the component walk on every re-read but check ownership, type and permissions only at startup
Apply none of the A17 checks after startup beyond A16’s four re-read checks
open_points.default_guess: Reapply every A17 opening and file-security check, refusing requests until a conforming read succeeds.

open_points.subject: A17 paths naming no component or an unopenable component
open_points.text: “a path that names no component, empty or `/` alone, a file that cannot be read; a component that cannot be opened so, for whatever reason, making the file one that cannot be read —”
open_points.question: What exact rule and refusal result does this grammatically incomplete clause impose, including for absolute paths consisting of multiple slashes and for configuration versus credential files?
options: Any path with no non-empty component is unreadable; configuration use refuses startup and credential use yields `credential_unresolved`
Only the literal path `/` is covered; other all-slash paths follow host pathname behavior
No-component paths have a distinct invalid-path refusal rather than being treated as unreadable
open_points.default_guess: Treat every path with no non-empty component as unreadable, with startup refusal for the configuration and `credential_unresolved` for a credential.

open_points.subject: A17 startup validation order
open_points.text: The change adds refusals for no or multiple command-line arguments, a non-absolute path, an unopenable component and several file checks, but gives no order among them or relative to the existing token, credential-header, data-directory and sandbox startup checks.
open_points.question: In what deterministic order are the new A17 startup checks performed, and which failure is reported when several startup conditions fail?
options: Argument count, absolute-path syntax, component opening, final-file checks, configuration parsing, then the other startup checks in a stated order
Perform all configuration checks before any other subsystem’s startup checks
Startup failure precedence is deliberately unspecified and only refusal is observable
open_points.default_guess: Check argument count, absolute-path syntax, component opening and final-file properties before parsing the configuration, then run the remaining startup checks in a fixed documented order.

open_points.subject: A20 Linux-only release boundary
open_points.text: “A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named” but “Another system ... is unsupported: the kernel neither tests for it nor defines what it does there.”
open_points.question: Does “on no other host” require the release or packaging to prevent execution on non-Linux hosts, or is it only a support statement under which the same artifact may start there with undefined behavior?
options: Linux-only packaging/build prevents installation or launch elsewhere, while the kernel performs no runtime platform probe
The artifact may start on another operating system, but all behavior there is undefined and unsupported
The kernel must refuse startup on a non-Linux host despite the statement that it does not test
open_points.default_guess: Make the release artifact Linux-only through packaging or build targeting, with no kernel runtime platform probe.
